# Disagreement Log — Gospel of Thomas, Saying 17

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Saying:** GTH 017
**Total Disagreements:** 3

---

## Disagreement 1 — "has arisen in the human heart" vs. "has occurred to the human mind" vs. "has entered any human mind"

**Verse:** v.1
**EMET:** "has never occurred to the human mind"
**LOGOS:** "has never arisen in the human heart"
**PNEUMA:** "has never entered any human mind"
**Issue:** Coptic *hēt* = heart; the seat of thought in Semitic idiom. "Heart" should be preserved. The verb of arising vs. occurring vs. entering differs. "Arisen in the heart" follows the Coptic's verbal metaphor best.
**Resolution (SOPHIA):** "Never arisen in the human heart" — LOGOS reading.

---

## Disagreement 2 — repetition of "ever" (PNEUMA)

**Verse:** v.1
**EMET/LOGOS:** "no eye has seen... no ear has heard..."
**PNEUMA:** "no eye has ever seen... no ear has ever heard..."
**Issue:** "Ever" is not in the Coptic and creates a slightly different emphasis. The Coptic absolute negation is sufficient.
**Resolution (SOPHIA):** No "ever" added; the Coptic negation stands on its own.

---

## Disagreement 3 — relationship to 1 Cor 2:9

**All agents:** All note the Pauline parallel
**Issue:** Should the consensus translation include a note about which version might be earlier (Thomas or Paul)?
**Resolution (SOPHIA):** Note included that Thomas's version adds "hand" (the tactile member) and may represent a more complete form of the tradition Paul cites. No claim about priority adjudicated.

---
